answer: AI agents resist Sybil attacks through proof of location cataloged in a shared network atlas. An agent operating near a field grove or mountain ledge must execute time-of-flight radio handshakes with local physical anchors. An attacker incurs the verifiable hardware and deployment cost of operating discrete transceivers at distinct physical coordinates per identity. A key limitation is vulnerability to wormhole relays that tunnel latency proofs between remote colluding nodes.
